chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Into the army; great players outlasting changes of style
summary: Collins went in as soon as war was declared and stayed four years; he notes great players like Roy remain great.

blocks.x: Then you went into the service, (Inaudible).
I went in the service as soon as they declared war that year they said John. Got me right away. And I stayed in for four years, just about four years.

But any way, the interesting thing is to see how the great players abridged all the style change, you know. There are some guys who just didn't make it, but they weren't great players, were they? I don't think so. You know. Well, I don't know -- why would I name names, you know. We don't name names like that. We wouldn't do that. All musicians are good, you know that. Of course you know all musicians are very good players.
Of course, but some are better than others,
That's right, that's the idea. But that's interesting, and coming back to Roy I stood and I
listened to Roy and Roy is still a great player. He is still a great player. It was -- it just amazed me you know. And now we'll come to John Collins now.
